analysis.investment_thesis: Latent View is a small but financially pristine data analytics firm — zero meaningful debt, consistent positive FCF, and clean operating margins near 19% — but ROE of 11.6% reflects a bloated cash-heavy balance sheet from its IPO, and the business lacks a discernible economic moat in a highly competitive analytics consulting market. Net profit grew only 9% in FY25 (₹173 Cr vs ₹159 Cr), and at 32x P/E for a consulting firm with no clear switching costs, the price is ahead of the fundamentals.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet: Debt/Equity of 0.02, positive OCF all 5 years, and FCF of ₹115 Cr on ₹848 Cr revenue — capital-light model is genuinely attractive
Revenue growing at solid clip (₹306 Cr in FY21 to ₹848 Cr in FY25, ~29% CAGR over 4 years) in a secularly growing data and AI services market
Operating margin of 18.58% is respectable for a services business and shows some pricing discipline
key_risks: ROE of 11.6% — well below my 15% threshold — reflects both a cash-heavy balance sheet and mediocre returns on deployed capital
Other income of ₹69 Cr (mostly interest on IPO cash) represents 40% of operating income — strip this out and the earnings picture is far less compelling
Client concentration in US tech sector creates significant revenue risk; any slowdown in tech spending (as seen in FY24 with net profit near flat) amplifies quickly
red_flags: Net profit growth near-stagnant: ₹155 Cr (FY23) → ₹159 Cr (FY24) → ₹173 Cr (FY25) — this is not the earnings power trajectory that justifies 32x P/E
No identifiable switching costs or network effects — analytics consulting clients can and do shop for price and capability each engagement
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Latent View passed through my financial health filter easily — the balance sheet is clean, cash flows are real, and the business does not destroy capital. What troubles me is the moat question: I cannot identify a durable reason why a Fortune 500 company would exclusively and permanently use Latent View over Mu Sigma, Tiger Analytics, or any of dozens of capable peers. Data analytics consulting is a people business with high attrition and low barriers to replication.

The financial optics are also somewhat misleading. Strip out ₹69 Cr of financial income from a ₹1,600 Cr cash pile sitting on the balance sheet (residue of its 2021 IPO), and operating profits are considerably thinner. The business is decent but ordinary — at 32x earnings, I am paying for a great business when I am getting an adequate one.
